title: Addition preserves prime-power and prime-multiple subring membership
statement: Let $p$ be a prime integer, $C$ a commutative ring, and $A\subseteq C$ a unital subring (a subset containing $1$ and closed under addition, multiplication, and additive inverses). Let $x,y\in C$ and let $n,m>0$ be integers with $x^{p^n},p^nx,y^{p^m},p^my\in A$. Then there exists an integer $a>0$ such that $(x+y)^{p^a},p^a(x+y)\in A$. Here integer multiples use the canonical $\mathbf Z$-algebra structure on $C$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], sending an integer $k$ to $k\cdot1_C$.
